_note: Visual semantic dictionary for the small visual elements in UWO that carry consistent meaning across screens — colored buttons, status indicators, attention badges, and other small graphical cues with stable interpretation.  Hand-authored from gameplay observation.  Read by perception code (where detectors exist) and by Claude-guided prompts as ground-truth context.  Pure data — no logic.  Add or refine entries here when a new indicator is observed or an existing one is found wrong; pure config — no code change required to update.

red_dot._note: Small filled red circle that overlays an icon or menu item when there is something the player should look at.  Universal 'needs attention' badge — same icon with vs without the dot is the SAME element, just in two different states.
red_dot.appearance: small filled red circle (precise pixel size to be measured — see open_questions)
red_dot.position: upper-right of the parent element.  For sub-menu items inside buildings the dot sits SLIGHTLY ABOVE the row of the menu item itself, in the upper-right corner.
red_dot.meaning: this item has pending content / a blocker requiring action / unread items / unclaimed rewards / a state-change worth investigating
red_dot.absence_means: no pending action for this item — does not necessarily mean 'all good', just that the game has nothing urgent to flag
red_dot.is_a_state_not_a_different_element: same element with vs without the dot is one entity.  Detection logic must NOT treat icon+dot and icon+no-dot as separate elements; the tap target and behaviour are identical.

appears_at.examples: mail icon shows the dot when there are uncollected rewards in the mailbox; perk_event icon shows the dot when a new perk or daily event is available; etc.

appears_at.location: main menu items (Guild, Auction, Combat, Collection, …) opened via top_right_icon_bar.icons[hamburger]
appears_at.examples: main-menu items receive the dot when their respective sub-system has new content / unread items / collectible rewards.  See ui_signals.json:main_menu_item_ids for the full list of main-menu items; the main_menu screen itself is not yet documented in ui_conventions.json (open_question).

appears_at.location: sub-menu items inside building screens (left-side menu list under the title)
appears_at.examples: the 'Recruit Crew' sub-menu item at the Inn shows the dot when the fleet has 'not enough crew'; presumably similar for other action-required sub-menus.

appears_at.location: tabs inside popups / dialogs (e.g. the 'Perk' and 'Event' tabs in the perk_event_popup title bar)
appears_at.examples: the perk_event_popup's Perk tab shows a red dot when there are unclaimed perks; the Event tab shows one when there are new events to view.  Same state-of-element semantics as elsewhere — not a separate tab, just a marked state.

red_dot.detection_approach: small red color blob (HSV around hue 0 / 175-179, saturation high, value medium-high) located at the upper-right corner relative to a known parent element bbox.  Detector implementation TODO; should be cheap (small kernel + red mask + corner constraint).
consumed_by: TODO — claude_guided_loop success criterion (e.g. recruit_crew dialog: red dot on Recruit Crew menu gone => action complete)
TODO — proactive maintenance loops (e.g. check mail icon for red dot daily and collect rewards)
currently used as a CONCEPT in Claude prompts but not as an automated detector

yellow_button._note: Primary positive-action button convention.  Whenever a screen requires the player to commit to an action, the action button is yellow (sometimes called gold).  Universal across all UWO buttons of this role.
yellow_button.appearance: solid yellow / amber rectangular button with text (and sometimes an icon — e.g. ducat amount for buy/sell/recruit cost)
yellow_button.size: varies by screen but typically a substantial primary-action button (>= 4000 px² at 2400x1080).  _find_yellow_button uses a MIN_AREA filter to avoid false positives on small yellow icons / decorations.
yellow_button.meaning: primary action — confirms or executes the player's intent on this screen
examples: Purchase / Sell (market basket and confirm dialogs)
Browse on arrival_panel_open_prompt (the 'enter the city now' button)
yellow_button.absence_at_expected_location_means: the action is currently unavailable — see disabled_grayed_button.  This 'absence-of-yellow' signal is what _ensure_fleet_ready uses as a fleet-not-ready check independent of any specific blocker text.
yellow_button.detection_approach: actions/sail_actions.py:_find_yellow_button — HSV mask, contour finding, minimum-area filter; supports optional region constraints (x_min, x_max, y_min, y_max) to disambiguate when multiple yellow buttons may appear
consumed_by: brain/recovery.py post-step adaptation (yellow button visible after tap_primary_action ⇒ guided loop fires)
brain/claude_guidance.py (visual_hint='yellow' in tap actions; resolved via _find_yellow_button before label-based search)

disabled_sub_menu_unusable_label._note: Conditional sub-menu items in the LEFT panel of building screens carry a small red 'unusable' label overlaid on the menu item when the sub-menu's precondition is not met.  Distinct from disabled_grayed_button (which applies to yellow primary action buttons) — this is the sub-menu version: same vertical-list position, but with a red text overlay indicating the sub-menu cannot be entered right now.
disabled_sub_menu_unusable_label.appearance: small red text label (e.g. 'unusable') rendered on top of or directly above the sub-menu item, plus the sub-menu text itself often rendering in a muted/red shade
disabled_sub_menu_unusable_label.appears_at: left-panel sub-menu items in any building screen — confirmed at the Inn's 'Hire' sub-menu when no unhired mates are currently visiting
disabled_sub_menu_unusable_label.meaning: the sub-menu's precondition is not met; tapping it will not navigate.  Investigate the precondition rather than retrying the tap.
disabled_sub_menu_unusable_label.tap_response: tapping a sub-menu in this state surfaces the disabled_sub_menu_tap_response_blue_ribbon transient message (see below) — does NOT navigate into the sub-menu.
disabled_sub_menu_unusable_label.consumed_by: TODO — pre-tap detector that masks 'unusable' sub-menus from consideration in the resolution planner

disabled_sub_menu_tap_response_blue_ribb._note: Transient post-tap message that fires briefly after tapping a sub-menu marked 'unusable'.  Informational; does NOT block subsequent input.  HARD to capture in a single OCR snapshot because the message is short-lived.
disabled_sub_menu_tap_response_blue_ribb.appearance: blue ribbon-like background with short text describing why the action was rejected (e.g. 'No mate to hire' when the inn's Hire sub-menu is tapped while no unhired mates are present)
disabled_sub_menu_tap_response_blue_ribb.duration: transient — appears for ~1-2 seconds and disappears
disabled_sub_menu_tap_response_blue_ribb.meaning: the sub-menu the user tried to enter is currently locked, with a brief explanation
disabled_sub_menu_tap_response_blue_ribb.implication: a single-frame perceive() may miss this entirely because of the short visibility window.  Multi-frame sampling around a tap is needed if the bot wants to read it.
disabled_sub_menu_tap_response_blue_ribb.better_path: the disabled_sub_menu_unusable_label on the sub-menu item itself is the AUTHORITATIVE pre-tap gate — bot should read THAT before tapping rather than relying on the post-tap blue ribbon.  This entry is documented so the bot can recognise the ribbon if captured (e.g. for diagnostic logging) but should not depend on it for control flow.

disabled_grayed_button._note: When a primary action is unavailable, the button is rendered desaturated/gray instead of yellow.  Tapping a gray button is a no-op (the original 'blind tap on Depart Now' bug spent minutes tapping nothing).
disabled_grayed_button.appearance: same shape and position as the yellow button it replaces, but with a desaturated gray fill
disabled_grayed_button.meaning: the action is currently unavailable — typically because of a blocker (insufficient crew/supply/funds, prerequisites not met, etc.)
disabled_grayed_button.implication: do NOT tap a gray button as if it were the yellow primary action — the tap will not do anything, and the bot will sit there waiting for state change.  Investigate WHY the button is gray (read surrounding context, check for blocking_signals from KB) and resolve the blocker first.
disabled_grayed_button.historical_significance: the bot's pre-FSM 'blind tap on Depart Now' era spent minutes tapping a grayed-out button with no awareness — see docs/journey_not_enough_crew.md prequel.  This indicator's existence is one of the most-load-bearing pieces of grammar in the game's UI.
disabled_grayed_button.detection_approach: two complementary signals: (a) ABSENCE of yellow at the expected button location is itself a signal — already used by _ensure_fleet_ready; (b) explicit gray-color detection in the same region.  (a) is what the bot currently relies on; (b) would be a future hardening if context-specific gray detection becomes useful.
consumed_by: actions/sail_actions.py:_ensure_fleet_ready — absence-of-yellow is treated as 'fleet not ready' signal even when no specific blocker text is matched
disabled_grayed_button.open_question: exact gray HSV range — currently the bot uses absence-of-yellow as the proxy.  If explicit gray detection becomes useful, the threshold range needs to be measured.

threshold_status_bar._note: Horizontal bar that displays both a fill level AND a state colour.  The COLOUR is the semantic signal — RED while the underlying value is BELOW a threshold (a blocker is active); GREEN once the value is AT OR ABOVE the threshold (no longer blocking).  This is NOT a fill gauge: 'green' does not mean 'full', it means 'sufficient'.
threshold_status_bar.appearance: horizontal bar with a fill that varies in length proportional to current/max, and a colour that varies based on threshold satisfaction

color_states.red: current value is BELOW the minimum threshold required for the action — blocker active
color_states.green: current value is AT OR ABOVE the minimum threshold — blocker resolved (the value need NOT be at maximum; just sufficient)

examples.red: ship below minimum crew → fleet cannot depart with this configuration
examples.green: ship at or above minimum crew → no longer blocking departure.  Note: minimum is sufficient for trade voyages; a FULL crew is only needed for combat, not trade.  So 'green' is the goal for the trade bot, not 'completely full'.

threshold_status_bar.key_distinction_from_a_progress_bar: a progress_bar (e.g. level XP) goes from empty to full and the colour is consistent throughout — it represents fill level.  A threshold_status_bar represents threshold satisfaction; the colour conveys the semantic, not the fill level.  The bar's length conveys the absolute value, the colour conveys whether it crosses the gate.
value_to_bot: the GREEN colour is the cleanest proximal success signal for blocker-resolution flows — once the per-ship bars in the recruit dialog turn green, the 'not enough crew' blocker is resolved without needing to re-navigate to the harbour to verify
the RED colour, conversely, is a clean signal that a blocker is still present even before reading any error text
threshold_status_bar.detection_approach: TODO — HSV color mask within a known bar region; classify as red vs green based on dominant hue (red ~0/175-179 vs green ~50-70).  The bar's bbox is parent-context-dependent (inside the recruit dialog the per-ship bars are stacked vertically in the right panel)
threshold_status_bar.consumed_by: TODO — claude_guided_loop local success check (cf. docs/journey_not_enough_crew.md F3 proximal verification discussion)
threshold_status_bar.open_questions: are there intermediate colour states between red and green (e.g. yellow/orange for 'caution but not blocking')?  Not yet observed — assumed binary red/green for now.  Worth verifying with other examples (supply bars, hull integrity, etc.)

task_completed_green_background._note: Translucent green background applied to an item in the task list when the task is finished and rewards are claimable.  Same family of state-overlay-on-existing-element semantics as red_dot — the row is the same row, the green background is the 'done, claim me' state.
task_completed_green_background.appearance: translucent green fill behind a task-list item; the underlying text and icon remain visible through the tint
task_completed_green_background.appears_at: the tasks tab in the right panel of port_overworld and sea_overworld (cf. ui_conventions.json:port_overworld.right_panel.tabs.tasks and sea_overworld.right_panel.tabs.tasks).  Same tab content, parallel structure across both overworlds.
task_completed_green_background.meaning: this task has been completed.  Tapping the row claims the rewards (and presumably removes or strikes-through the row afterwards).
task_completed_green_background.absence_means: the task is not yet completed — neutral background.
task_completed_green_background.interaction_value: the bot can periodically scan the tasks list, identify any rows with the green background, and tap each to harvest free rewards.  Combined with the mail-icon red-dot scan, this is the second 'free passive income' loop the bot can run.
task_completed_green_background.is_a_state_not_a_different_element: same row, two states (neutral vs done).  Detection should treat them as one element.
task_completed_green_background.detection_approach: TODO — translucent green HSV mask within the task-tab item region.  'Translucent' means the bar is detectable by colour but at lower saturation than a solid green button or threshold bar — threshold tuning may need adjustment.

progress_bar._note: Linear fill bar that goes from empty to full as a value approaches its maximum.  Distinct from threshold_status_bar — the colour is FIXED (does not change to convey state) and only the fill length conveys the value.
progress_bar.appearance: horizontal bar with a coloured fill that grows from one end as a numeric value increases toward maximum
progress_bar.color: ALWAYS YELLOW for the only progress bar observed so far (the player level XP bar).  Yellow here is part of the bar's visual identity — distinct from yellow_button which means primary-action.  The progress bar is much thinner and longer than a button, so visual confusion is unlikely.
examples: player level progress (current XP toward next level) at the bottom-center of sea_overworld — see ui_conventions.json:sea_overworld.player_ship_overlay.level_progress_bar.  This is the only progress bar observed so far.
progress_bar.meaning: progress toward a target — typically not action-relevant in the short term; useful for long-term tracking
progress_bar.consumed_by: TODO — periodic capture into a progression log when growth tracking is implemented
progress_bar.open_question: are there other progress bars beyond the level XP bar?  Combat / mate skill / expertise bars likely exist but have not been observed in this round.

shrouded_with_spinning_lights._note: Visual indicator placed on the sea_overworld at a port's position when the fleet has spotted the port from a distance but not yet visited it.  Pairs with the 'Oh, a new port!' sailor speech bubble.  Same port renders as ??? on the world_map until first visit (see world_map.port_discovery_state).
shrouded_with_spinning_lights.appearance: small icon at the port location surrounded by spinning / animating light effects
shrouded_with_spinning_lights.meaning: a new port has been detected at this position but not yet entered
shrouded_with_spinning_lights.interaction: tap to set sail toward the port; or sail manually close enough to see the on-screen 'Enter New City' label
shrouded_with_spinning_lights.detection_approach: TODO — geometric (bright animated lights at port-icon positions on sea_overworld).  Animation makes single-frame detection less reliable; multi-frame sampling may be needed.

fog_of_war_cloud._note: World_map overlay covering sea regions the fleet has not yet sailed into.  Documented structurally in ui_conventions.json:world_map.fog_of_war.
fog_of_war_cloud.appearance: cloud-textured overlay obscuring the underlying coastlines and ports
fog_of_war_cloud.behavior: permanent — sailing into a clouded region uncovers it for good and the cloud does not return
fog_of_war_cloud.detection_approach: TODO — likely a low-saturation high-brightness color blob detection on the world_map view.  Distinguish from the open sea (which is also high-brightness but more saturated and has visible features).
fog_of_war_cloud.consumed_by: TODO — exploration logic and route planning when implemented

highlighted_sub_menu_item._note: Inside building screens, the currently-selected sub-menu item has a visual highlight.  Subtle and not always reliably detectable; the SCREEN TITLE change is the more reliable signal of which sub-menu is active.
highlighted_sub_menu_item.appearance: subtle background or accent change on the selected item — exact treatment varies by building type and may not be uniform
highlighted_sub_menu_item.meaning: this is the currently active sub-menu / tab
highlighted_sub_menu_item.more_reliable_alternative_signal: screen_chrome.screen_title.behavior — the title changes to the sub-menu's name when one is selected.  Title comparison is the canonical signal.  The visual highlight is at best a redundant hint; lean on the title.
highlighted_sub_menu_item.exception: the Shop screen does NOT change the title on sub-menu selection (see ui_conventions.json:screen_chrome.screen_title.known_inconsistency_in_shop) — the visual highlight may be the only available signal there.
highlighted_sub_menu_item.detection_approach: low priority for general use; specific implementation only needed for the Shop exception when that becomes relevant
